Lymphadenopathy

tempo and laterality sort every neck node · acute and unilateral is bacterial · covering staph, strep, anaerobesHow fast did the node appear, on one side or both, and which organisms must the drug cover?

1Script2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Presentation
Bottom line
  • Sort an enlarged node by site, tempo and side: one acute, unilateral, tender, warm, red neck node in a young child is bacterial lymphadenitis (Staphylococcus aureus, then Streptococcus pyogenes), treated with clindamycin.
  • Bilateral, small, mobile nodes with a current URI (upper respiratory infection) are reactive: observe. A node that grows over weeks is cat-scratch disease when tender and draining a scratch, or nontuberculous mycobacteria when painless and violaceous.
  • Malignancy flags: supraclavicular, firm or immobile, larger than 2 cm without infection, generalized, or with systemic symptoms; these get a CBC and chest radiograph, not observation, and a firm, immobile or enlarging node, or one that persists longer than six weeks, goes on to biopsy.

Nodes swell where they drain: a neck node reports on the throat, mouth and scalp, and an arm node on a scratch farther down the limb. An acute hot node is the node itself infected; reactive nodes are many and small; malignant nodes in children are usually painless. In practice: a small node with no flags is rechecked after 10 to 14 days on the board answer; another reference allows up to 4 weeks of observation when there are no other findings.

2Urgent risks
Act now
FindingPoints toAction
Fever, neck pain, drooling or a muffled voice with a tender nodeCT of the neck, then drainage with antibiotics (Deep Neck Infections covers it).
Nontender nodes with bruising, pallor, bone pain or hepatosplenomegalyCBC with a smear now (Acute Leukemia in a Child covers the marrow test).
Fever for 5 days or more with a unilateral cervical node, red eyes, rash, strawberry tongue or swollen handsCount the criteria: fever plus 4 of the 5 (Kawasaki Disease covers the workup and treatment).
3Differential
Acute neck swelling, over days
DiagnosisDecides itNext best step
Bacterial lymphadenitis (acute unilateral cervical lymphadenitis)Under age 5; one acute, unilateral, tender, warm, red node, often 3 to 6 cm, with or without fever; S. aureus, then S. pyogenes; oral anaerobes after age 5 with poor dental hygiene.Empiric clindamycin, which covers S. aureus including MRSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus), S. pyogenes and oral anaerobes; fluctuance adds incision and drainage. In practice: guideline authors, on expert opinion, also accept a 10-day oral course of cephalexin or amoxicillin-clavulanate; the board answer is clindamycin.
Reactive viral adenopathyBilateral, small, mobile, mildly tender nodes during a current URI; shotty nodes.Supportive care and observation.
Infectious mononucleosis (EBV, Epstein-Barr virus)Fatigue, fever, pharyngitis, posterior cervical nodes and hepatosplenomegaly.Heterophile (monospot) test.
Infected thyroglossal duct cystFever with midline neck pain that worsens with swallowing or tongue protrusion; the cyst rises with the tongue.Ultrasound first; Sistrunk excision, but not during the acute infection.
Infected branchial cleft cystCystic lateral mass anterior to the sternocleidomastoid, sometimes with a draining pit; does not move with swallowing; flares after a URI.Refer for excision once the infection is treated.
Tularemia (Francisella tularensis)Rabbit, tick or deerfly contact; an ulcer with a black base and a regional node.Examine the entry site for a black-based ulcer and take an animal and tick history.
A node over weeks, or a red flag
DiagnosisDecides itNext best step
Cat-scratch disease (Bartonella henselae)A papule at a cat scratch, then a tender regional node proximal to it, on its drainage path, within 2 weeks, axillary most often, then cervical; may suppurate; fever in some; fails drugs aimed at S. aureus and S. pyogenes.Ask about cats; often clinical, and Bartonella serology confirms; generally self-limited, and azithromycin speeds recovery. In practice: adult references often skip antibiotics for localized disease in a healthy host and give azithromycin to shorten it.
Nontuberculous mycobacterial adenitisAge 1 to 5; a chronic, painless, violaceous submandibular node in a well child.Excisional biopsy, which usually also treats it.
A chronic, single, usually cervical, nontender node with TB (tuberculosis) risk.Tuberculin skin test or interferon-gamma release assay, then node biopsy with acid-fast culture.
ToxoplasmosisBilateral, symmetric, nontender nodes after cat exposure.Send Toxoplasma serology.
HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)Generalized painless nodes.HIV antigen/antibody test.
LymphomaClassically Hodgkin lymphoma: firm, nontender cervical or supraclavicular nodes, or a mediastinal mass, may be the first sign; fever and night sweats.CBC and chest radiograph, then excisional biopsy.
Disseminated histoplasmosisLung disease with mediastinal nodes, or hepatosplenomegaly with generalized nodes, mostly in the immunosuppressed; Mississippi and Ohio River valleys.Order Histoplasma testing for that picture only, never for a single hot node.
4Workup
Clues that change the answer
CluePoints toNext best step
Cat scratches, but midline neck pain worse on swallowing or tongue protrusionInfected thyroglossal duct cyst, not cat-scratch diseaseUltrasound, then Sistrunk excision after the infection settles.
Eastern Arkansas or a river valley, one hot neck nodeBacterial lymphadenitis; the geography is a decoyGive clindamycin and skip Histoplasma testing.
Caries or poor dental hygiene in a child over 5Oral anaerobes beside S. aureus and S. pyogenesGive clindamycin, which still covers all three.
A resolved URI a week before the nodeThe portal of entry, not reactive adenopathyTreat the single hot node as bacterial.
Recurrent skin abscesses, osteomyelitis or pneumoniaDihydrorhodamine test (Neutrophil Disorders: Number and Function covers it).
Pause point
Child with fever and anterior neck pain, scratches from the family cat Offered as cat-scratch disease or infectious mononucleosis Is the pain midline and worse with swallowing or tongue protrusion? → Infected thyroglossal duct cyst; the cat is a distractor
Teen on clindamycin for a red lump at the elbow, now tender axillary nodes and fever Offered as interferon-gamma release assay or HIV test Is the node tender, regional and draining a skin lesion, and did antistaphylococcal therapy fail? → Cat-scratch disease: Bartonella serology
Toddler from eastern Arkansas with one hot, 5 cm neck node and fever Offered as itraconazole or supportive care One acute hot node, or lung disease with organomegaly? → Bacterial lymphadenitis: clindamycin
Practice
  1. 3 yo M with a 5 cm tender, warm, erythematous, poorly mobile right anterior cervical node appearing over 2 days, T 38.6, with a resolved upper respiratory illness a week earlier → Clindamycin → covers MRSA, S. pyogenes and anaerobes
  2. 4 yo with a 1.5 cm mildly tender unilateral cervical node, afebrile, well-appearing, no overlying erythema → Supportive care with reassessment → small, afebrile and not red: observe and recheck in 10 to 14 days
  3. 3 yo who has taken clindamycin for 48 hours whose node is now fluctuant with spreading erythema → Incision and drainage with continued antibiotics → suppuration has developed
  4. 8 yo with a 3-week history of a slowly enlarging tender axillary node and a papule where his kitten clawed him → Cat-scratch disease → azithromycin
  5. 3 yo with a 6-week painless violaceous submandibular node, afebrile and otherwise well → Nontuberculous mycobacterial adenitis → surgical excision
  6. 7 yo with poor dental hygiene and acute unilateral bacterial cervical lymphadenitis in a community where MRSA is uncommon → Cefdinir → no coverage of oral anaerobes, which poor dental hygiene brings
  7. 5 yo from the Mississippi River Valley with cough, mediastinal lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly and diffuse adenopathy → Disseminated histoplasmosis → amphotericin B, as for any disseminated histoplasmosis
  8. 2 yo with fever, cough and rhinorrhea with bilateral small mobile mildly tender cervical nodes → Reactive viral adenopathy → supportive care
  9. 4 year old with 1 day of fever and a red, tender, fluctuant 2 cm anterior cervical node; normal dentition, no animal contact, no rash → Staphylococcus aureus → With Streptococcus pyogenes – acute, unilateral, suppurative
  10. Child with acute unilateral cervical adenitis and extensive dental caries → Anaerobic oral flora → Prevotella and relatives follow periodontal disease
  11. Child with acute unilateral cervical adenitis after skinning a rabbit → Francisella tularensis → The exposure names the organism
  12. Child with bilateral tender cervical nodes, coryza and pharyngitis for 3 days → Acute viral adenitis → Bilateral and acute points at adenovirus and its relatives
  13. 3 yo with cough and rhinorrhea last week, now resolved, and a single neck node noticed yesterday that is 4 cm, tender, warm and red today; T 38.5 → Acute bacterial lymphadenitis → empiric clindamycin
  14. 12 yo M with a painful left neck lump a week after a febrile URI, now cystic, with a small pit anterior to the sternocleidomastoid draining mucopurulent fluid → Branchial cleft cyst → second-arch remnant infected after a URI; resect cyst and tract
  15. 8 yo with a tender midline neck cyst after a cold that rises when she sticks out her tongue → Thyroglossal duct cyst → follows the path of thyroid descent from the foramen cecum
  16. Adult trumpet player with a soft lateral neck swelling that enlarges when he bears down → Laryngocele → laryngeal mucosa pouching through the thyrohyoid membrane, inflated by pressure
  17. 16 yo F with a tender red lump at the left elbow 5 days ago, diagnosed as lymphadenitis and treated with clindamycin taken as prescribed; now fever and increasing swelling in the left armpit; T 38.3; a 1 cm tender mobile epitrochlear node and several 2 to 3 cm tender left axillary nodes; no other enlarged nodes → Bartonella henselae serology → cat-scratch disease; ask about cats; azithromycin speeds recovery
  18. 24 yo F who adopted a stray cat 2 months ago, with 3 weeks of fatigue and low-grade fever; 1 to 2 cm nontender, mobile posterior cervical nodes on both sides, symmetric; no pharyngitis, no splenomegaly, no skin lesions; heterophile antibody test negative → Toxoplasmosis → Toxoplasma serology; self-limited in an immunocompetent adult
  19. 26 yo M who moved from the Philippines 2 years ago, with a single firm, nontender, 3 cm right cervical node that has enlarged slowly over 2 months; no pain, no overlying warmth, no animal exposure; other node regions normal → Tuberculous lymphadenitis → interferon-gamma release assay, then node biopsy with acid-fast culture
Decoy note The location, eastern Arkansas, is genuinely endemic for histoplasmosis. Mentioned in a stem beside relatives with colds, it reads as an exposure history. It is not one: sick contacts explain a recent URI. The location explains nothing, because histoplasmosis does not present as a single hot node.
Congenital neck masses, sorted by location Midline, moves with swallowing or tongue protrusion – thyroglossal duct cyst, often found after a URI · Midline, does not move with the tongue – dermoid cyst, along an embryologic fusion plane · Lateral, anterior to the sternocleidomastoid, below the mandible – branchial cleft cyst, usually second arch, between the internal and external carotids; cured by resecting the cyst and its tract · Lateral, necrotic node with violaceous skin and a fistula – nontuberculous mycobacterial adenitis · Posterior triangle, from birth or on prenatal ultrasound – cystic hygroma · Lateral, enlarges with Valsalva – laryngocele, through the thyrohyoid membrane; often in wind-instrument players · Submandibular sinus draining sulfur granules – actinomyces, after dental infection or trauma
Pearls Tempo and laterality sort neck nodes before anything else – acute and unilateral is bacterial, chronic and unilateral is Bartonella or mycobacterial, acute and bilateral is viral · Clindamycin is chosen for its spectrum, not its class – a cephalosporin that misses MRSA and oral anaerobes can fail · Violaceous and nontender is mycobacterial, and its preferred treatment is surgical excision rather than antibiotics · Fluctuance adds drainage – the drug stays the same · A resolved URI a week earlier is a portal of entry, not a competing diagnosis; a concurrent URI would point at reactive adenopathy instead
Pairs with Respiratory Infection in a Child covers pharyngitis and reactive nodes with a URI.
Deep Neck Infections covers retropharyngeal and peritonsillar abscess.
Kawasaki Disease covers prolonged fever with a unilateral cervical node.
Acute Leukemia in a Child covers nontender nodes with cytopenias.
Tuberculosis covers tuberculous lymphadenitis.
Neutrophil Disorders: Number and Function covers chronic granulomatous disease.
How NBME framed it Scratches from a pet cat were placed beside a cat-scratch disease option, but acute midline pain that worsens with swallowing or tongue protrusion names an infected thyroglossal duct cyst.
Transferable rule When every option is a drug, name the organisms you must cover, then find the single agent that covers all of them. A geographic detail matters only when the syndrome matches the endemic disease, not merely the location.
Unchecked attributeSupportive care only: observation suits an afebrile child with a small, minimally tender node; a child with a temperature of 38.6 C and a 5 cm inflamed node is at risk of abscess.
Unchecked attributeAzithromycin: correct for cat-scratch and part of mycobacterial therapy, but both are chronic and indolent, unlike a node that appeared yesterday.
Class-vs-memberCefdinir: covers S. pyogenes but not MRSA or oral anaerobes, and the organisms cannot be told apart at the bedside.
Salient decoyItraconazole: eastern Arkansas is histoplasmosis country, but histoplasmosis presents with pulmonary or disseminated disease, not an isolated hot node.
True-fact-wrong-slotOseltamivir: influenza adenopathy is bilateral and accompanies active respiratory symptoms, not a URI that has already resolved.
